title: The Twelvefold Way
key_idea: The **Twelvefold Way** (Rota's term) systematically classifies the 12 cases of distributing $n$ **balls** into $k$ **boxes** according to three binary choices: balls labeled or unlabeled, boxes labeled or unlabeled, and occupancy restricted (injective/surjective/unrestricted). Each case gives a standard combinatorial sequence: $k^n$, $k!S(n,k)$, $\binom{n}{k}$, $p_k(n)$ (partitions into $k$ parts), etc.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** The 12 cases are: $f: N \to K$ with $N,K$ labeled/unlabeled and $f$ unrestricted/injective/surjective. Organized in a 3×4 table. Key counts: $k^n$, $k!S(n,k)$, $S(n,k)$, $\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, $\binom{n-1}{k-1}$, $p(n,k)$, $p_k(n)$, $\binom{n}{k}$, $n!/k!$... and Stirling numbers of both kinds.
